stem: Meera watches the Moon from her balcony in Jaipur at 8 p.m. on Monday and sees it low in the eastern sky. Her grandmother says that on Tuesday at 8 p.m. the Moon will look different. What should Meera predict?

options.text: The Moon will be in the same place at 8 p.m. because it always follows the Sun's daily schedule.
The Moon will be in a different part of the sky and will rise later than it did on Monday.
The Moon will rise exactly at sunset every day, so its position cannot change.
The Moon will not be visible at all on Tuesday because it disappears after one night.

teacher.key_rationale: Because the Moon advances in its orbit while Earth rotates, it returns to nearly the same sky position about 50 minutes later each day, so its time and place in the sky shift day by day and it does not always rise at sunset. Option B states this prediction; A and C assume the Moon follows the Sun's daily schedule, and D is factually false.
